classification.difficultyReason: Recover missing prism dimensions, recognising when equal edge marks require a cube root instead of division.

content.prompt: Find the missing value for each pronumeral.

spec.description: Tall cuboid, pale upright face, left and bottom faces; depth displaced down-left.
spec.mathematics: Cuboid with projected basis vectors u=(1.6,0), v=(0,2.8), w=(-0.85,-0.48). Explicit visible faces ABCD, ADHE and AEFB. Camera exposes the upright, left and bottom faces; other edges are obscured. Dimensions 4 km, 2 km and x km; volume 72 km³.
spec.answerVisibility: Unknown x and given volume only.

spec.description: Low cuboid with front, top and right faces and up-right depth.
spec.mathematics: Projected orthogonal cuboid basis u=(2.4,0), v=(0,0.9), w=(0.7,0.55). Visible faces ABCD, DCGH and BFGC; hidden rear-left edges omitted. Given height 3 cm, depth 2 cm, length x cm and volume 48 cm³.
spec.answerVisibility: Unknown x and given volume only.

spec.description: Cube with square face, right face and bottom face; down-right depth and three matching single ticks.
spec.mathematics: Equal physical edge lengths along three axes. Projection u=(1.8,0), v=(0,1.8), w=(0.75,-0.75). Visible faces ABCD, BFGC and AEFB. Equality ticks at the midpoints of AD, DC and CG are perpendicular to their projected edges. Volume 216 cm³.
spec.answerVisibility: Unknown x and given volume only.

answer.worked:
The matching marks show that all three dimensions are equal.
$$\begin{align*}V&=lwh\\216&=x\times x\times x\\x^3&=216\\x&=\sqrt[3]{216}\\x&=6\ \mathrm{cm}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Cube with darker front, lighter top/right faces and up-right depth; three matching single ticks.
spec.mathematics: Equal physical edge lengths along three axes. Projection u=(1.8,0), v=(0,1.8), w=(0.9,0.9). Visible faces ABCD, DCGH and BFGC. Midpoint equality ticks on AB, BC and CG are perpendicular to the respective projected edges. Volume 27 m³.
spec.answerVisibility: Unknown x and given volume only.

answer.worked:
The matching marks show that all three dimensions are equal.
$$\begin{align*}V&=lwh\\27&=x\times x\times x\\x^3&=27\\x&=\sqrt[3]{27}\\x&=3\ \mathrm{m}\end{align*}$$
